q: I’m exhausted and on the verge of tears everyday. Rewards, punishments, taking things away don’t seem to help. I’m desperate.
cx: 3.5-year-old pees on the floor daily since a baby arrived seven weeks ago; preschool in September.

q: I tried introducing new foods, tried to eat meals with him but nothing works. Though he has been playful and drinking his milk both day and night but I am worried that he’s not receiving the decent amount of calorie intake per day. I feel like a bad mom. :(
cx: Mother of a 19-month-old who eats only rice, bread, yogurt and egg since new teeth came in.

q: NOTHING is working and I am so fed up. Any help will be greatly appreciated (please no criticism, I know we screwed the pooch on this one)
cx: Almost-4-year-old not trained; a difficult younger sibling took the attention.

q: Cousins (same age) are fully able to potty completely alone. Everyone around us is a success story and we are just not
cx: Same parent, the comparison with family.

q: And no, us parents are revolving each other for work schedules and our support network is thin at best
cx: Answering whether they can do a dedicated training stretch.

q: Everyone talks about consistency in the beginning stages and how you gotta bring the kiddo to the bathroom every 30min or hour. How do you do it if you are always out and about?
cx: A 2-year-old who melts down at home; standard advice assumes staying in.

q: We don’t have a backyard. I tried to have him play around the neighborhood (riding bikes, playing bubbles, etc) but he was over it and wanted to go someplace. I live in Los Angeles where you gotta drive everywhere and it’s a 10-15min one way drive just to the market.
cx: Same parent on why staying home does not work for them.

q: I’m so ashamed of ”failing”. I’m so ashamed when I see other kids younger than her running around without a diaper.
cx: Almost-4-year-old who now screams at the sight of a potty after an illness.

q: I left because I really want daycare to work but I’ve felt sick ever since.
cx: 12-month-old's first full day; still screaming 15 minutes after drop-off.

q: How long should I/would you give it before calling it quits?
cx: Same parent the same day.

q: It's crazy how quickly all reason flies out the window as soon as I hear her cry.
cx: Same parent agreeing with a commenter.

q: In the world of gentle parenting and co-regulation (which I am all for), I feel like a failure for not being able to regulate myself better.
cx: Stay-at-home mother of an almost-3-year-old with meltdowns and potty struggles, and a clingy baby.

q: Like my patience is at zero and I have to have my husband handle any bedtime battles or wake ups because I just respond in anger now.
cx: Same mother by the end of the day.

q: Does it ever get better? Is there something wrong with me? How do other people regulate better?
cx: Same mother asking strangers.

q: I am trying SO HARD to be patient and be happy and keep my voice regulated, but NOTHING is working
cx: Stay-at-home mother of a 1-year-old who hits, bites and throws himself down; a newborn followed.

q: I just feel like I have not had a single break and I’m literally exhausted
cx: Same mother.

q: my mum always tells me I can’t “palm him off”
cx: Young single mother whose 21-month-old sleeps well for a friend; her own mother objects.

q: But my mum just makes me feel so guilty for doing so
cx: Same mother on her mother's reaction.

q: I honestly neglect my own basic needs every single day I never have the time and after a few weeks of no sleep it gets too much and I just need a day or 2 alone to be myself not a mum.
cx: Same mother defending the occasional break.

q:
Do you think it’s ok to start or he’s not ready yet?   
And what’s your advice on pull ups vs just underwear or commando? Method that worked for your boy?
cx: First-time mother of a 26-month-old reading readiness signs.

q: Admittedly, my parents and MIL are not the best at entertaining kids and will default to screentime after a while to keep him entertained.
cx: 3-year-old clings to his father, then to the other parent; grandparents babysit rarely.

q: We tried preschool a month ago and ended up not liking the place, so we’re actively searching for a new one. He was there for 3 hours and it was really traumatic for him.
cx: Return-to-office mandates force childcare; the first preschool trial went badly.

q: I have mentioned his separation anxiety to the pediatrician before and she does not think it’s abnormal. She thinks it’s just his temperament + a product of a kid who is always with his parents.
cx: The paediatrician's view.

q: It was so embarrassing because all the other babies had apparently conspired to be perfect angels on this particular day.
cx: Water-loving 2-year-old screamed through her first swim lesson among babies.
